Senate Republicans strip $1 billion in funding for security upgrades to the proposed White House ballroom from a revised budget reconciliation bill.[384]
Arizona reports its first death of the Sin Nombre strain of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome.[385]
Actor James Handy is killed in his Los Angeles home following a fatal stabbing wound. The son of Handy's girlfriend is later arrested.[386]
Gallup releases a poll saying support for same-sex marriage in the U.S. has declined after two decades of growth, with 65% of adults saying it should be legal, down from 71% in 2022 and 2023.⁠[387][388]
June 4
The Kennedy Center orders staff to remove all references to Donald Trump's name from the building following a court ruling.[389][390]
Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes says she will seek new indictments against fake electors involved in attempting to overturn the 2020 election in the state following a denial of an appeal by Mayes that would require prosecutors to send the case back to the grand jury.[391]
The U.S. House passes legislation to provide new aid to Ukraine and new sanctions on Russia.[392]
ICE ends a Biden-era policy to report detainee deaths that occur within 30 days of leaving custody.⁠[393]
June 5
Federal judge John McConnell Jr. strikes down the Trump administration's policy that halted asylum and green card proceedings for applicants from 39 countries. The ruling states ICE's actions are arbitrary and capricious and ignore the law.[394][395]
The National Football League's Chicago Bears vote to advance plans for stadium development in Hammond in northwest Indiana to replace Soldier Field as its home stadium. However, the site of the stadium still remains determined.[396]
The FDA says that Target has recalled two types of baby wipes due to bacterial contamination.[397]
NASA orders four astronauts of the Crew-12 mission to prepare to evacuate the International Space Station due to an air leak on Russia's Zvezda service module. The order is rescinded two hours later as the air leaks are sealed.[398]
Energy Secretary Chris Wright announces a nuclear microreactor developed by Antares Nuclear at the Idaho National Laboratory reached criticality, a milestone for the Trump administration's development of nuclear energy.[399]
NBC News reports that the Pentagon raised the threat of Israeli spying on the U.S. to the highest level; Israeli and American officials deny the veracity of the report.[400]
June 6 – Iran war: The United States military strikes Iranian coastal radar sites after shooting down Iranian drones launched towards the Strait of Hormuz. Iran responds by launching missiles and drones towards U.S. military facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait.[401][402]
June 8
Federal judge Leo Sorokin voids President Trump's $100,000 fee requirement for H-1B visa applications, ruling that Trump lacked congressional authority to impose what amounted to a tax on the programme.[403]
The Kennedy Center removes Donald Trump's name from the building following the ruling.[404]
A U.S. Army Apache helicopter crashes near the Strait of Hormuz. The crew is rescued safely.[405]
Trump attends Game 3 of the NBA Finals, becoming the first sitting president to do so.[406]
Trump nominates Todd Blanche to serve as the U.S. attorney general, where he currently serves in an acting capacity.[407]
The U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform releases a report accusing Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison of being aware of widespread fraud in federally-funded social programs.[408]  Vance refers both officials to the Department of Justice for criminal fraud investigation.[409]
June 9
Controversial candidate Graham Platner wins the Democratic primary for the US Senate election in Maine.[410]
Iran war: The U.S. military launches new strikes against Iran in response to the downing of a U.S. Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz, further straining a fragile ceasefire.[411]
June 10
Trump quips "I love inflation" despite inflation reaching a three-year high of 4.2%, up from 3.8% a month earlier, driven by rising energy costs.[412]
Trump signs legislation providing nearly $70 billion to fund ICE and the Border Patrol through the remainder of his term, ending a nearly six-month dispute over Department of Homeland Security funding.[413]
2026 NBA Finals: In basketball, the New York Knicks rally from a 29-point deficit to beat the San Antonio Spurs 107–106 in Game 4, taking a 3–1 series lead in the NBA Finals after OG Anunoby tipped in the game-winning basket with 1.2 seconds remaining. The comeback is the largest in NBA Finals history, surpassing the 24-point comeback from the Boston Celtics in Game 4 of the 2008 NBA Finals.[414]
The Florida Supreme Court declines to block a new Republican-drawn congressional map from being used in the midterm elections. The map could enable Republicans to gain as many as four additional seats in the U.S. House.[415]
June 12: Elon Musk becomes the first and only US dollar trillionaire.
June 11 to July 19 – The United States is co-hosting the 2026 FIFA World Cup alongside Canada and Mexico and hosting the majority of games during the tournament, including all games past the quarterfinals of the knockout stage including the final, which will be held at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
June 11
Trump nominates US Attorney Jay Clayton as the Director of National Intelligence, withdrawing his nomination for Bill Putte amid congressional pushback.[416]
The U.S. becomes the world's biggest exporter of oil, surpassing Russia and Saudi Arabia, amid the trade disruptions caused by the wars in Ukraine and Iran.[417]
June 12
Elon Musk's SpaceX makes the largest-ever stock market debut, with a valuation of more than $2 trillion, making Musk the first and only US dollar trillionaire.[418]
2026 FIFA World Cup: The U.S. men's national soccer team wins its opening match, 4–1, against Paraguay in the FIFA World Cup in SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.[419]
The U.S. Department of Commerce issues an export control directive requiring Anthropic to suspend access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 artificial intelligence models by foreign nationals, citing national security concerns. Anthropic disables the models for all users in order to comply.[420]
Trump announces that an American strike killed Niño Guerrero, the "terrorist" leader of Venezuelan transnational organized crime syndicate Tren de Aragua. Trump states that the military action was coordinated with the Venezuelan acting president Delcy Rodriguez.[421]
June 13
2026 UFL season: In American football, the Louisville Kings defeat the DC Defenders, 27–20, to win their first United Bowl championship in their inaugural year in the United Football League.[422]
2026 NBA Finals: In basketball, the New York Knicks defeat the San Antonio Spurs 94–90 in Game 5 of the NBA Finals to win their first championship title since 1973 and their third overall. They also become the first team out of the four major league teams in the New York metropolitan area to win a championship since the New York Giants in 2011.[423]
Trump's name is removed from the Kennedy Center.[424]
June 14
Iran war: Trump and Iran announce that they have reached an agreement to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump also says that he has authorized the lifting of the US naval blockade of Iran. The US military later clarifies that the blockade will remain in effect until the agreement is signed on 19 June.[425][426]
2026 NBA Finals:
Police arrest 63 people outside Madison Square Garden in New York City after 10 police officers were injured during celebrations of the New York Knicks winning the NBA Finals.[427]
Gunshots are reported overnight on 42nd Street and Broadway in New York City with one teen shot and several buses being damaged during celebrations.[428]
The UFC Freedom 250 event, named after the 250th anniversary of the U.S. Declaration of Independence, is held on the South Lawn of the White House. The event coincides with Trump's 80th birthday.[429]
June 15
Iran War: US Vice President JD Vance announces that the Islamabad Memorandum was digitally signed by the US and Iran the previous day.[430]
Eight people are killed in a B-52 bomber crash in California.[431]
June 16 – SpaceX announces a US$60 billion all-stock deal to acquire Cursor, the developer of the AI coding assistant Cursor, with the transaction expected to close in the third quarter of 2026.[432]
June 17
Iran war:
The Pentagon reveals that xAI's Grok model was utilized by the US during the war.[433]
Trump states that if he does not like the agreement with Iran, the United States will "go right back to dropping bombs".[434]
Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian sign a memorandum of understanding to end the war. Trump signs the document at the Palace of Versailles, during a dinner with French President Emmanuel Macron following the G7 summit.[435]
2027–2028 United States redistricting: Republicans in the Georgia General Assembly reject an attempt by Governor Brian Kemp to redistrict Georgia's congressional districts for the 2028 U.S. House of Representatives elections in the state after State House Speaker Jon G. Burns announced that he will not hold a vote to do so.[436]
June 18
MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak: Two more passengers who were on the MV Hondius cruise ship during the hantavirus outbreak exit the National Quarantine Unit at the University of Nebraska Medical Center in Omaha, Nebraska, bringing the total number of people remaining in quarantine to six.[437]
After over 35 years in service, the U.S. Air Force retires the Boeing VC-25A aircraft used as Air Force One.[438]
The Barack Obama Presidential Center is dedicated in Chicago, with all living former presidents except Trump in attendance.[439]
June 19
Trump officially unveils the Qatari-gifted Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews.[440]
The Department of Justice opens an investigation into Major League Baseball (MLB) after the league warned three San Francisco Giants players for writing Bible verses over their rainbow logo caps before a  Pride Night game.[441]
June 21
MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak: The last American passenger exits the National Quarantine Unit at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, officially ending the quarantine for Americans who were affected by the hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship.[442]
The Washington Post publishes an investigation into Tulsi Gabbard's relationship with Chris Butler and the Science of Identity Foundation, alleging that confidential memos from her congressional career showed outside political and policy guidance. Gabbard's office and representatives of the foundation reject the report, calling the allegations false and anti-Hindu bigotry.[443]
June 22 – In college baseball, the Oklahoma Sooners baseball team defeat the North Carolina Tar Heels to win the College World Series for the first time since their 1994 season.[444][445][446]
June 23
Iran war: The Senate, by a vote of 50–48, mandates the United States to either end its war operations or seek congressional consent to continue fighting.[447]
2026 NBA draft: The 80th edition of the NBA draft is held at the Barclays Center, with the Washington Wizards selecting former Brigham Young University (BYU) freshman AJ Dybantsa with the first-overall pick.[448]
The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act passes in the United States House of Representatives, sending it to President Trump for his signature.[449]
June 24 – President Trump cancels a planned signing ceremony for the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, saying that he will not sign the bill until Congress passes the unrelated SAVE America Act, a voter identification and proof-of-citizenship bill.[450][451]
June 25
2026 Utah wildfires: Utah Governor Spencer Cox announces a state of emergency and temporary restrictions on fireworks through the Fourth of July weekend until July 5 due to ongoing wildfires in the state, including the Cottonwood Fire.[452]
In Mullin v. Al Otro Lado, the U.S. Supreme Court rules 6–3 that migrants stopped on the Mexican side of the U.S.–Mexico border have not "arrived in the United States" for the purposes of federal immigration law, allowing the federal government to revive its "metering" policy for asylum seekers at border crossings.[453]
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis confirms that the Alligator Alcatraz detention center in Ochopee, Florida, will close operations, a year after it opened.[454]
June 26 – Former national security adviser John Bolton pleads guilty to improperly retaining classified material.[455]
Flash floods hit Kentucky, leaving four dead.[456][457]
June 27
Iran war: The US military announces that it struck Iranian military surveillance infrastructure, communication systems, air defense sites, drone storage facilities, and minelayer capabilities at the commander-in-chief's direction in retaliation for an alleged Iranian attack against a ship in the Hormuz.[458]
Trump nominates Lance Schroyer, former Oklahoma State trooper, as ICE Director.[459][460]
June 28 – Iran war: The U.S. and Iran agree to stop the exchange of attacks between them.[461]
June 29
In Trump v. Slaughter, the US Supreme Court rules 6–3 that the president may remove Federal Trade Commission commissioners at will, overturning the 1935 precedent set by Humphrey's Executor v. United States and expanding presidential removal power over independent regulatory agencies. In a separate 5–4 ruling in Trump v. Cook, the Court leaves in place an injunction blocking Trump's attempted removal of Federal Reserve Board of Governors member Lisa D. Cook, holding that Federal Reserve governors retain for-cause removal protections.[462][463]
The Supreme Court declines to hear President Trump's appeal of a $5 million civil judgment in E. Jean Carroll v. Donald J. Trump, leaving in place a jury verdict finding him liable for sexually abusing and defaming writer E. Jean Carroll.[464]
Former American football running back Chris Johnson announces in an interview on the Good Morning America that he has been diagnosed with ALS.[465][466]
June 30
Iran war: Iran announces that it was unable to export any oil during the US blockade of its ports.[467]
In Trump v. Barbara, the US Supreme Court rules 5-4 that birthright citizenship is guaranteed under the Fourteenth Amendment and strikes down Trump's Executive Order 14160.[468][469] Justice Kavanaugh concurs that the executive order should be struck down, but he believes that birthright citizenship is in federal statutory law rather than the Constitution.[470]
In West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox, the US Supreme Court rules 6–3 that states may ban transgender athletes from participating in women and girls' sports.[471][472]
In National Republican Senatorial Committee v. FEC, the US Supreme Court rules 6–3 that federal limits on political parties for campaign finance violate the First Amendment's Free Speech Clause and strikes down those provisions in the Federal Election Campaign Act.[473][474]
Ford issues a recall order of over 741,000 vehicles, mainly F-150, Explorer, Expedition, Lincoln Aviator, and Navigator models, due to a transmission issue that may damage the park system.[475]
July[edit]
July 1
Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announces that the US will not renew the USMCA free trade agreement signed during Trump's first administration.[476]
Trump takes his first flight in the new Air Force One, which was gifted by Qatar.[477]
Three American soldiers are injured and one soldier is missing after their MH-60S Seahawk helicopter went down in the Arabian Sea.[478]
July 3
2026 North American heat wave: Heat waves are reported across the eastern and central United States, with Independence Day celebrations cancelled or postponed including the Great American State Fair on the National Mall.[479] Around 23 U.S. states are placed under heat warnings by the National Weather Service.[480]
A man dies after setting himself on fire outside the UN in New York, with activists and reports identifying him as a pro-Tibet advocate.[481]
Democrat Harry Benton resigns from the Illinois House of Representatives after allegations of misconduct.[482]
USS Billings in New York Harbor's Sail250 during the United States Semiquincentennial celebration.
July 4
July 4 – The U.S. celebrates its semiquincentennial, in recognition of the 250th anniversary of the 1776 adoption of the United States Declaration of Independence from Great Britain.[483]
The Department of Government Efficiency officially shuts down operations.[484]
July 5
The Navy suspends its search for one of its missing soldiers in the Arabian Sea.[485]
2026 FIFA World Cup: FIFA suspends the automatic one-match ban given to United States forward Folarin Balogun following his red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina, allowing him to play in the round of 16 against Belgium, after President Trump personally urged FIFA president Gianni Infantino to review the case. The decision is criticised by UEFA and the Royal Belgian Football Association.[486][487]
July 6
2026 United States Senate elections: Amidst ongoing controversies surrounding U.S. Senate nominee Graham Platner (D-ME) including a recent sexual assault allegation, Platner says that he will consider "taking the time" to consider his next steps in the race.[488]
2026 FIFA World Cup: Co-hosts United States are eliminated from the tournament after losing 4–1 to Belgium in the round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle.[489]
July 7 – Amidst ongoing speculation regarding the health of U.S. Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY), spokespersons for Republican leaders including U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune and U.S. Senate Republican Whip John Barrasso say that McConnell has spoken with them.[490][491]
July 8
2026 United States Senate elections: U.S. Senate Democratic Party nominee Graham Platner suspends his campaign in the upcoming U.S. Senate race in Maine amidst ongoing controversies surrounding his campaign, leaving the party to seek a replacement challenger to incumbent Republican Susan Collins.[492][493]
Iran war: The interim ceasefire between the United States and Iran breaks down after Iranian attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Trump declares the agreement "over", while saying that negotiations may continue.[494][495][496]
At the 2026 NATO summit in Ankara, Trump says that he has ordered Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to halt all U.S. trade with Spain, calls Spain a "terrible partner" in NATO amid disputes over Spain's defense spending and the Iran War, and declares that the US will provide Ukraine a license to build Patriot missiles.[497][498]
July 9
The U.S. Department of Justice announces that a federal grand jury has indicted eight men over an alleged plot to attack the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in Washington, D.C. last month.[499]
The proposed 2 World Trade Center breaks ground in Lower Manhattan in New York City, 25 years after the original building was destroyed during the September 11 attacks.[500][501]
July 10
2026 United States Senate elections: Graham Platner officially withdraws from the Senate race in Maine, with the Maine Secretary of State's Office confirming his withdrawal.[502]
The Trump administration loosens export controls on the UAE.[503]
July 11
Housing in the United States: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a piece of legislation passed in the U.S. Congress to expand affordable housing and reduce housing costs in the United States, becomes law after U.S. president Donald Trump allows the bill to take effect without his signature.[504][505]
Iran war: Iran's IRGC navy says that it has closed the Strait until further notice after firing a warning shot at a vessel trying to transit through an unapproved route.[506]
Republican U.S. senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina dies at his home in Washington, D.C., aged 71, following a brief and sudden illness. His death creates a vacancy in the United States Senate, with Governor Henry McMaster to appoint a temporary successor ahead of a special Republican primary to replace Graham as the party's nominee in the November election.[507][508]
July 13
2026 Iran war: Trump announces that the US will reinstate the "Iranian blockade in the Strait of Hormuz" and impose a 20% toll on cargo shipping through the strait.[509] American-led Combined Maritime Forces' Joint Maritime Information Centre (JMIC) announces that the US naval blockade on Iran will start the following day.[510] Trump formally informs the US Congress that the country has renewed hostilities against Iran.[511]
South Carolina Governor Henry McMaster appoints Darline Graham to finish the remainder of Lindsey Graham's term.[512]
The Trump administration begins a diplomatic push to "dismantle" the International Criminal Court.[513]
A cyclosporiasis outbreak, caused by cyclospora cayetanensis, is reported in 31 U.S. states, with the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reporting 2,640 cases in the state.[514]
An officer from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement fatally shoots 26-year-old Colombian national Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero during an attempted vehicle stop in Biddeford, Maine. Guerrero, who had authorization to work in the United States, was not the person ICE had intended to apprehend. The shooting is investigated by state and federal authorities.[515]
July 14
2026 Iran war: Trump cancels plans to impose fees in the strait.[516]
Trump administration officials tell ICE officers to suspend most vehicle stops following the fatal ICE shootings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Houston, Texas and Biddeford, Maine, respectively. Both shootings occurred after ICE agents pulled over a vehicle and shot the driver.[517] However, Trump and Markwayne Mullin reverse this position the next day.[518]
Trump pays E. Jean Carroll $6.5 million, three years after being found liable of sexually assaulting her in the E. Jean Carroll v. Donald J. Trump lawsuit.[519]
New York becomes the first state to impose a moratorium on data centers.[520]
July 16 – The Wisconsin Department of Health Services reports the first hospitalization of the summer in Wisconsin in connection with the cyclosporiasis outbreak.[521]
July 17: demolition begins on the historic Medical Arts Building in Chattanooga, Tennessee.
July 17
Taylor Farms recalls all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico after federal health officials link shredded lettuce supplied by the company and served at Taco Bell restaurants in five states to an outbreak of cyclosporiasis that infects at least 1,644 people and hospitalizes 94.[522][523]
Demolition begins on the historic 146 ft (45 m) tall, art deco Medical Arts Building in Chattanooga, Tennessee despite preservation efforts. It was designed by Reuben H. Hunt.[524]
July 18 – Social media personalities Andrew and Tristan Tate are arrested by the U.S. Marshals Service in Miami following a British request for their extradition. The brothers face charges in the United Kingdom including rape, assault and human trafficking, while Andrew also faces offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Both deny the allegations.[525]
July 19 – 2026 FIFA World Cup final: Spain beat defending champions Argentina 1–0 after extra time at the MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey to win a second FIFA World Cup title.[526]
July 20 – 2026 Iran war: The U.S. military conducts a ninth consecutive night of strikes on Iranian targets, which President Trump says are retaliation for the deaths of three American soldiers.[527]
July 21
The US announces a trade agreement with Jordan.[528]
The US begins allowing direct flights between the US and Lebanon for the first time since 1985.[529]
OpenAI reveals that an autonomous artificial intelligence agent powered by its models escaped a controlled testing environment and compromised the computer systems of Hugging Face while attempting to obtain answers to a cybersecurity evaluation. OpenAI describes it as an "unprecedented cyber incident".[530][531]
July 22
2026 Iran war: The US conducts its 11th consecutive night of strikes in Iran.[532] Trump states that the US would strike and destroy Iran's bridges and power plants for each ship it attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.[533]
The U.S. signs a deal with Saudi Arabia to develop a civilian nuclear program in the country.[534] Trump demands that Saudi Arabia join the Abraham Accords so that the agreement will take effect.[535]
July 23
2026 Iran war: The US conducts its 12th consecutive night of strikes in Iran.[536][537] The American military uses a B-1 long-range bomber to strike IRGC targets in Iran for the first time since fighting with Iran resumed 12 days prior.[538] The US House approves a symbolic legislation instructing Trump to cease US military action against Iran, but the Senate backs Trump.[539]
Several people are reported to have died from a Legionnaires outbreak in New York City, while several dozen have been infected over the past month.[540]
United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer imposes tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on most imports from 60 major trading partners, including China, the United Kingdom and the European Union, citing their failure to adequately restrict imports produced using forced labour. The countries and territories affected account for 99.4% of US imports.[541]
Vance Boelter is sentenced to two life terms without parole for killing Minnesota state representative Melissa Hortman and her husband and wounding state senator John Hoffman and his wife in June 2025.[542]
July 24 – The FDA approves a non-prescription, fixed-dose pill combining Tylenol and naproxen for pain relief in alignment with Trump's healthcare plan to make safe pharmaceutical drugs available over-the-counter.[543]
July 25 – 2026 Iran war: US forces cease overnight strikes against Iran after 13 nights of attacks.[544][545]
July 27
Three people are killed and four others are injured, including a 2-year-old boy in a shooting at a food festival in Seattle.[546]
The Office of the Attending Physician says that Senator Mitch McConnell remains in a rehabilitation facility and has not been medically cleared to return to the Senate, more than six weeks after being hospitalized following a fall. McConnell is undergoing multiple daily physical therapy sessions but gives no timetable for his return and says he will miss Kentucky's annual Fancy Farm Picnic.[547][548]
July 30
The US awards Lockheed Martin a record $58.6 billion contract to manufacture Patriot missile interceptors, as the Middle Eastern crisis and the Russo-Ukrainian war reduced global US military armament stocks.[549][550]
The Trump administration informs Congress that it is sending over $206 million for International Stabilization Force.[551]
Iran war:
The US military states that it carried out dozens of retaliatory strikes targeting the IRGC in Iran.[552]
Cyberwarfare during the Iran War: Minnesota IT Services reports a cyberattack across 30 municipal community water systems in Minnesota, with authorities believing Iranian hackers were probably responsible. The water supply is found to still be safe to drink.[553][554]
July 31
Trump orders the military to undertake massive military strikes against Iran, which may begin as early as that weekend and last for several days, in order to push the Iranian regime to negotiate.[555]
The DOJ drops their criminal case against former olympian David Hearn for vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.[556] Instead, the DOJ acknowledges that damage to the Reflecting Pool was caused by botched installation from Trump's chosen contractor, Atlantic Industrial Coatings. The following day, Trump criticizes the DOJ's decision on Truth Social.[557]
August[edit]
August 1
A mass shooting occurs at an In-N-Out in Twin Falls, Idaho, leaving four dead (including the perpetrator) and seven injured.[558]
The Marine Corps reports that an F-35B stealth warplane crashed in California, but the pilot bailed safely.[559]
Cyberwarfare during the Iran war: The New York Times reports, citing state and local officials, that evidence leads to Iran in a series of cyberattacks against water systems in at least seven US states, with Michigan being the second state to report the attacks publicly.[560]
August 2 – 2026 Iran war: Following Qatari diplomatic efforts to avert planned strikes and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and concerns raised by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman over the proposed operation,[561][562] Trump says that the United States and Israel have called off an attack on Iran after Tehran requested additional time to reach an agreement. Trump nevertheless stresses that the United States remains prepared to launch a large-scale bombing campaign against Iran.[563][564]
August 3 – The Supreme Court declines to halt a $655 million judgement against Palestinian authorities for attacks that killed and maimed Americans in Israel from 2002 to 2004.[565]
August 4 – The Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) announces that the expansion team in Cleveland, Ohio, will be called the Sirens. The organization will debut in 2028.[566]
August 5
Drive-thru chain Salad and Go files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and closes all 70 of its locations across Arizona and Nevada, citing the 2026 cyclosporiasis outbreak as part of the reason for declining business.[567]
The leveraged buyout of Electronic Arts is completed, with a consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and including Silver Lake and Affinity Partners acquiring the American video game publisher for US$55 billion and taking it private. The transaction is the largest leveraged buyout in history.[568]
The Senate confirms Dr. Erica Schwartz as the director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to succeed acting director Dr. Jay Bhattacharya.[569]
August 6
A Republican-led US Senate committee votes to hold former Chief Medical Advisor to the President Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress, escalating efforts to blame him for potential COVID-19 pandemic mistakes.[570]
United States Senator Mitch McConnell is discharged from a rehabilitation center after more than seven weeks of recovery following a June hospitalization. He will continue recovering at home while remaining away from the Senate.[571]
A judge in New Mexico orders Meta Platforms to pay an additional $567 million in penalties over five years for liability in knowingly harming children's mental health.[572]
August 7
A sweeping Russia sanctions bill negotiated by the late Senator Lindsey Graham is passed by the Senate to force Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the Russo-Ukrainian war.[573]
US opens test ranges for small companies to receive munitions faster.[574]
Former U.S. president Joe Biden's son Hunter says in a BBC interview that Biden's prostate cancer has metastasized into his bones and further.[575][576]
August 8
The Senate confirms Todd Blanche as the United States attorney general to succeed Pam Bondi.[577]
The United States Department of Defense asks the US defense sector to accelerate the manufacturing and delivery of armaments, including ammunition that is in short supply because of the 2026 Iran war.[578]
Royce White becomes the second former NBA player, after Enes Kanter Freedom, to declare that they are eligible for the 2027 WNBA draft.[579]
August 9 – 2026 cyclosporiasis outbreak, salmonellosis in the United States: Taylor Farms extends its recalls to products containing jalapeños after they were linked to the ongoing salmonellosis outbreak in the United States. Taylor Farms currently has a recall for iceberg lettuce linked to cyclosporiasis.[580][581]
August 10 – Staff secretary Will Scharf is named as White House counsel by Trump.[582]
August 11 – US rights organizations sue Trump over sanctions against the ICC.[583]
August 12
A Pentagon assessment finds that US strikes targeting the Houthis killed 153 civilians in Yemen over the past year.[584]
A total solar eclipse occurs at the Moon's descending node of the orbit in North America and Europe. The total eclipse passes over the Arctic, Greenland, Iceland, the Atlantic Ocean and northern Spain.[585]
Trump announces that White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt will leave the office at the end of the month to spend more time with her family.[586]
2026 Iran war: US media reports that sailors on the Abraham Lincoln attempted to jump overboard owing to poor conditions such as food shortages, a mental health crisis, and broken toilets that affected all crew members, including female soldiers. Pete Hegseth, the US secretary of defense, denounces the sailors as liars.[587] The US eventually opts to send the aircraft carrier USS George Washington  to the Middle East to replace the Lincoln, removing its last aircraft carrier in the Pacific.[588][589]
August 13 – The United States sees the first triple execution on the same day, since 2010.[590]
August 14
Six people are killed, including the perpetrator, and one person is injured in a mass shooting at three different locations in Missaukee County, Michigan.[591]
2026 NFL season: The National Football League suspends Atlanta Falcons linebacker James Pearce Jr. for eight games in violation of the league's personal conduct policy after his arrest in February on domestic violence charges.[592][593]
August 15 – The Democratic National Committee votes to approve South Carolina as the first U.S. state of the 2028 presidential primaries cycle for the Democratic Party in the upcoming presidential election.[594][595]
August 17
Trump orders the Pentagon to reduce yearly joint exercises with South Korea, saying that Seoul  refused to help with the 2026 Iran war and citing his good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.[596]
The 60-day deadline for the US and Iran to negotiate a "final deal" to end the 2026 Iran war expires.[597][598] Following the official end of the US-Iran ceasefire, Trump urges Iran to surrender.[599]
August 18
The Defense Department orders an audit of 30 universities' partnerships with foreign institutions, most of which are Chinese, but also include Russian and Iranian institutions.[600]
President Tomoko Akane of the International Criminal Court and a senior trial lawyer at the court who was part of a team which sought an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleged war crimes in the Gaza war is sanctioned by the US.[601]
The national debt surpasses $40 trillion for the first time.[602][603]
August 19 – Jessica Bowie, a 35-year-old woman, is arrested over an alleged Islamic State-inspired terrorist attack on the New York State capital.[604][605]
August 20
Declaring "economic D-day," Trump announces that any nation trading with Iran will be sanctioned.[606]
Reuters reports that more than 150 Polymarket wallets may have traded using non-public U.S. military information.[607]
The Asia-based USS George Washington replaces Abraham Lincoln.[608]
August 22
The Trump administration informs Congress that it intends to pay $850 million of the several billion dollars it owes the UN, the highest payment the administration has made to the international body since demanding major reforms in exchange for ongoing support as its largest donor.[609]
50% tariffs are imposed by the Trump administration on Canadian exports.[610]
A court in New York overturns the Trump policy of suspending the processing of immigration visas from 75 nations.[611]
Far-right activist Jake Lang, who was pardoned last year for his role in the January 6 riot at the United States Capitol, is arrested during a protest in Minneapolis, Minnesota.[612]
August 23 – The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is held at the National Mall as part of the United States Semiquincentennial celebrations.[613]
August 24
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announces a new U.S. sanctions campaign against the Iranian government dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, warning that every country has a set deadline to halt economic activities with the government identified by Washington or risk Treasury action that includes the removal of the US dollar financial system.[614][615] Hegseth refuses to rule out US military force against it.[616]
Syria is removed by the US Department of State from its State Sponsors of Terrorism list.[617]
Nearly 90,000 people are told to evacuate as a wildfire approaches Reno, Nevada.[618]
August 25: Dolly Parton dies at the age of 80 from cancer.
August 25
Ghislaine Maxwell loses her attempt to overturn her sex trafficking conviction.[619]
Country singer-songwriter, philanthropist, actress, and businesswoman Dolly Parton dies from cancer at the age of 80.[620][621]
August 26
Meta agrees to a $17.1 billion settlement over claims brought by 29 states that its platforms harm children.[622]
Palestine Action is designated by the US as a terrorist organization.[623]
The FDA approves the new daraxonrasib drug by Revolution Medicines to treat pancreatic cancer. Studies and testing found that patients taking the drug nearly doubled their survival time with fewer side effects.[624]
SpaceX and Louisiana governor Jeff Landry co-announce a plan to build a $100 billion spaceport on 125,000 acres (51,000 ha) of land in Vermilion Parish.[625]
The US military schedules a trial date for the suspected 9/11 mastermind Khalid Sheik Mohammed in 2028.[626]
The Trump administration authorizes its ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa to hold talks with Hezbollah.[627]
August 27
Incidents at Six Flags parks: The X2 roller coaster at the Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park in Valencia, California, closes after two riders were recently hospitalized for brain injuries including hemorrhages.[628][629]
The US states it disrupted a Chinese hacking campaign that targeted the Justice Department, NASA, the Federal Reserve, the Senate, and other important government entities.[630]
Trump signs an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America" in federal agency usage.[631]
August 28
Protests against Donald Trump: demonstrators gather in Washington, D.C. at the March on Washington 2026: Defend the Vote rally to protest against the Trump administration's efforts to roll back voting and civil rights, 63 years after the March on Washington rally by Martin Luther King Jr.[632]
2026–27 NHL season: in ice hockey, the Colorado Avalanche sign defenceman and alternate captain Cale Makar to an eight-year extension worth $163.2 million, the largest contract in National Hockey League history. He is the first player to exceed $20 million in AAV (average annual value).[633][634]
Trump announces the establishment of a "Space Academy" to train future civilian and military recruits.[635]
Richmond, Virginia removes the last three Confederate statues, with the three removed are statues of Stonewall Jackson, former Governor William Smith, and Hunter McGuire.[636][637]
The US Treasury declares that it has cut off all Banque Misr's UAE branches from dollar transactions due to its dealings with the Iranian government.[638]
August 29
Trump declares that the US reached a deal with Venezuela for controlling 65 billion barrels of its oil reserves.[639]
The former White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez is ordered by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to pay $172,000 for using advance access to Trump's speeches to make illegal betting on prediction-market platform Kalshi.[640]
A federal court in California rules that Trump cannot deport students who criticize the Israeli war in Gaza.[641]
American singer Olivia Rodrigo holds the inaugural charitable Daisy Chain Fields music festival in Irvine, California, a day after announcing that the festival would donate $10 million to organizations contributing to women's rights and reproductive justice.[642]
August 30
NASA launches the flagship Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Designed to investigate dark energy, dark matter and exoplanets, the observatory has a field of view at least 100 times larger than the Hubble Space Telescope's.[643][644]
U.S. forces state that they targeted two Iranian launchers on Larak Island after IRGC forces were identified preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines toward the Strait of Hormuz.[645]
August 31
Iran claims to have retaliated by attacking U.S. bases in Jordan and U.S. military assets in the United Arab Emirates.[646]
The Pentagon signs seven-year agreements with General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems and Lockheed Martin to boost production quantities and expedite delivery schedules for critical missile subcomponents supporting THAAD and Patriot missiles.[647]
Murder of Tupac Shakur: former gang leader Duane "Keffe D" Davis is found guilty of murder with a deadly weapon for orchestrating the 1996 drive-by shooting of rapper Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas, marking the first conviction in the nearly 30-year-old case.[648]
A fatal stabbing in Times Square kills one person and injures another.[649]
September[edit]
September 1
Following reports of tensions with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, US Army Secretary Daniel P. Driscoll steps down.[650]
The U.S. announces that it struck IRGC targets in Iran after the latter's attacks on commercial shipping in Hormuz and its soldiers, adding that it targeted tankers owned by the National Iranian Oil Company as part of its new "tanker to tanker" policy.[651][652]
Over $560,000 in cryptocurrency donations for Hamas are seized by the Justice Department.[653]
LGBTQ rights in the United States: The Department of Justice files a lawsuit against the Kansas City Public Schools district over its policies that allow transgender students to share their preferred name, gender, and pronouns with school staff.[654]
September 2
Birthright citizenship in the United States: American federal judge Deborah Boardman of the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland blocks an attempt by the Trump administration to implement an executive order aimed at ending birthright citizenship in the United States.[655][656]
Hegseth extends the deployments of approximately 50,000 American soldiers in West Asia, which include warship crews, air defense units, and paratroopers, until 2027.[657]
September 3
Chipmaker Nvidia agrees to buy the Hugging Face AI platform in a deal worth $12.9 billion.[658]
The United States House of Representatives passes a bill to curb university boycotts of Israel.[659]
OpenAI launches GPT-6, the next major version of ChatGPT.[660]
The National Fish and Wildlife Foundation announces $1.2 million in grants to reduce the extinction risk for Hawaiian forest birds and restore essential watershed habitats in Hawaii.[661]
September 4
The US military announces that it had disabled ad trackers on devices following reports that commercially available location data had been used to target its soldiers in the Middle East.[662]
The judge in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, a mother accused of murdering her three children, says he will declare a mistrial.[663]
The US Treasury announces that it has cut off Turkish investment bank Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi and two subsidiaries from dollar transactions because of their dealings with the Iranian government.[664]
The price of diesel hits an all-time high of $5.85 per gallon, compared to an average of $3.71 a year ago and exceeding the previous high following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.[665]
September 5
The US military reports that it destroyed three IRGC-connected oil tankers in response to the latter's fire on its warships.[666]
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meet Russian president Vladimir Putin in Moscow to deliver a proposal to end the war in Ukraine.[667]
In college football, ESPN College GameDay announces the inaugural "Hall of Fan" award, with the Ol' Crimson flag from the Washington State Cougars as its first inductee.[668]
In high school football, Lahainaluna High School and Paradise High School host a football game known as the Unity Bowl in Maui to bring both communities together. Both communities were devastated by the 2018 Camp Fire and 2023 Hawaii wildfires, respectively.[669]
September 6
A measles outbreak in Pennsylvania, concentrated in Lancaster County's Mennonite communities, becomes the nation's largest outbreak, with 577 cases statewide and 246 confirmed in the county; state officials had reported two measles-associated deaths in Lancaster County in August, Pennsylvania's first since 1991.[670][671]
At least five people are killed in an Amazon Air cargo aircraft crash at Miami International Airport.[672]
September 8 – Former president Joe Biden announces that the radiation treatment he received for prostate cancer last fall "worked as intended" and that doctors helped in disease control.[673]
September 9
The US announces that it destroyed five Iranian tankers in retaliation to additional attempted missile attacks on one of its Navy warships.[674]
The price of oil exceeds $100 per barrel for the first time since July.[675]
Trump promises a $5,000 "Trump dividend" to every adult US citizen if the Republican Party retains control of both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections. The proposal, which could cost $1.3 trillion and would require congressional approval, raises legal questions because the payments are conditional on a Republican electoral victory.[676][677]
Lawmakers from both parties call for stronger regulation of artificial intelligence after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigns, warning that the race towards superintelligence could threaten human survival by the end of the decade. Senator Bernie Sanders says he will introduce legislation to pause AI development and ban superintelligence, while Representative Ted Lieu calls for passage of the bipartisan AI Kill Switch Bill.[678][679]
September 11
The United States marks the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks with memorial ceremonies across the country. Vice President JD Vance and all four living former presidents – Bill Clinton, George W. Bush, Barack Obama, and Joe Biden – attend the ceremony at the World Trade Center site, while President Donald Trump attends a separate ceremony at the Pentagon.[680]
The Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority votes to rename the Nashville International Airport after Dolly Parton, almost a month after she died following a private battle with cancer.[681]
An Afghan woman who was a lawful permanent resident of the US and was accused of supporting the Islamic State is deported by the U.S. Department of Justice, marking the first use of the Alien Terrorist Removal Court in 30 years.[682]
A black male suspect is arrested over the death of a black woman found hanged from a tree in Mississippi.[683]
September 12 – The sheriff's office of Washington County, Tennessee, announces that the remains of the last victim of Hurricane Helene were found, two years after the hurricane hit East Tennessee.[684][685]
September 13
Trump dismisses concerns over the rapid pace of AI research, following days of warnings from experts in the field about possible existential risks.[686]
In a meeting with US officials, the Houthis promise not to attack American or any other commercial vessels, with the exception of those belonging to Saudi Arabia.[687]
September 14
The yield on benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury notes rises above 5% for the first time since October 2023, amid a global bond sell-off as surging oil prices and disruption to Middle Eastern energy supplies fuel renewed fears of inflation. The yield reaches 5.01%, while Brent crude rises above $108 a barrel.[688][689]
U.S. Senator Mitch McConnell returns to the Senate floor following a three-month absence.[690]
Trump announces that he is willing to engage with Iran to negotiate a deal.[691]
Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding celebration is reported to have been partly funded by a Russian oligarch with close connections to President Vladimir Putin.[692]
A court in Boston blocks Trump restrictions on how long foreign students and journalists can remain in the country.[693]
The Supreme Court rejects the Trump administration's request to lift an injunction blocking new United States Postal Service restrictions on mail-in voting ahead of the midterm elections.[694]
The US Space Force announces that the country now has weapons deployed in orbit, suggesting that the unspecified platforms are needed to compete with adversaries China and Russia.[695]
September 15
The US military announces that it destroyed two Iranian small boats the day before following an IRGC attempt to capture one of its Navy drones patrolling the Strait of Hormuz.[696]
A federal judge blocks the Kennedy Center from adding President Trump's name to the building or its grounds without congressional approval. Hours later, the centre's board votes to close most of the venue for up to two years for renovations.[697][698]
September 16
Three people are killed in a helicopter crash in Chatsworth, Los Angeles, including NBC News journalists Eliana Moreno and George Marciniw.[699][700]
The Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time in three years, from 3.5%-3.75% to 3.75%-4%.[701]
A memorandum of understanding is signed with the Pakistan army by US drone maker Powerus, which is set to merge with a firm backed by Trump's sons.[702]
The Trump administration announces that Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas and his delegation are barred from attending the UN General Assembly in New York, accusing them of breaching US law.[703]
September 17
The House of Representatives passes sweeping Russia sanctions legislation by a vote of 262–159.[704]
Flash flooding in the Navajo Nation kills three.[705]
A UN mission finds grounds to believe that the US committed war crimes in the 2026 Minab school attack and the 2026 Lamerd sports hall attack.[706]
Lockheed Martin receives the first batch of Patriot interceptor parts from General Motors less than a month after the two companies signed a manufacturing agreement, in a success for the Pentagon's push for faster weapon production, particularly the Patriot missile defense system, as it remained one of the world's most sought-after weapons for the US war in Iran and Russia's war in Ukraine.[707]
The US sanctions Iranian financier Babak Zanjani's cryptocurrency exchange for enabling the Iranian government and processing payments for ships to safely transit through the Strait of Hormuz.[708]
The US announces that it will restrict "luxury splurge" shopping by the Iranian government during the UN General Assembly.[709]
The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation approves a debt facility worth up to $414 million for Canadian miner Global Atomic's Dasa project in Niger, which the company describes as the highest-grade uranium deposit in Africa.[710]
September 18
Russia and China veto a US proposal for UN experts to continue monitoring UN sanctions on Iran over its nuclear program.[711]
The US sentences a Syrian national who fraudulently immigrated to the country and served as the former head of the notorious Adra Prison under former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad to 60 years imprisonment on torture charges.[712]
Trump bans CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news."[713]
Greenland crisis: The United States, Denmark and Greenland announce an agreement to strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic, expanding the permanent U.S. military presence in Greenland while recognising Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination. The agreement follows months of threats by President Trump to acquire or annex Greenland.[714][715]
September 19
The Trump administration approves a potential $2.68 billion sale of air defense equipment to Ukraine, adding that the country would finance it using a combination of European contributions and US foreign military financing.[716]
Trump signs the "Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026," which allows him to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on Russian oil buyers, including China and India, in response to the country's war in Ukraine, as well as to extend existing sanctions on Iran.[717]
The United States Southern Command states that its strike on a vessel in the Caribbean killed four people, adding that confirmed intelligence indicated the vessel's active participation in narco-trafficking.[718]
Sanctions against Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki's People's Front for Democracy and Justice and Eritrean forces are lifted by the Trump administration "to advance US regional interests" in the Red Sea.[719]
September 22 – The cybercrime group ShinyHunters claims to have breached the Federal Bureau of Investigation's jobs portal and stolen personal data belonging to thousands of current and former FBI employees and job applicants. The FBI opens an investigation, while Reuters partially verifies a sample containing names, addresses, Social Security numbers and details of sensitive intelligence assignments.[720][721]
September 23
Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian arrives in New York to speak at the United Nations General Assembly, the first time an elected leader from a nation at war with the United States sets foot on American soil to address a UN gathering.[a][722]
Movie magnate Harvey Weinstein is sentenced to 15 years in prison after being convicted of sexually assaulting former TV production assistant Miriam Haley in 2006 at his Manhattan apartment.[723]
September 24
A federal judge rules that Trump's White House ban on journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico likely breached the First Amendment and due process clause and orders access to be reinstated.[724]
The Navy confirms that eight sailors from the USS Lincoln group, which spent a record-setting amount of time at sea in support of the Iran war, attempted suicide.[725]
Iraqi authorities announce that the US transferred the diplomatic and logistics hub at Baghdad International Airport to Iraq prior to the withdrawal of American soldiers from the country.[726]
Chinese leader Xi Jinping meets Trump at the White House during his first visit to Washington in a decade. The two leaders discuss trade, artificial intelligence, Taiwan and international conflicts, and agree to extend the existing US–China trade truce by two months.[727][728]
September 25 – Cities and states across the U.S., including Lexington, Nashville, New Orleans, and Portland, hold commemorations honoring former American country singer Dolly Parton including the 9 to 5 song one month after her death. California becomes the first U.S. state to designate September 25 as Dolly Parton Day.[729][730][731]
September 26
A powerful nor'easter strikes the northeast United States. A New York City Housing Authority employee is killed by a falling tree in Brooklyn.[732]
Trump rejects Iran's seven-day ceasefire proposal over nuclear concerns.[733][734]
September 28
SpaceX's Starship achieves orbit for the first time, and deploys 26 "next generation" Starlink V3 satellites.[735]
OpenAI announces that it will cancel the release of GPT-6.1, the next version of ChatGPT amid ongoing safety concerns. The company also issues an update on recent incidents during which its AI model hacked into other websites.[736]
Secretary of State Marco Rubio orders that the Iranian delegation to the UN General Assembly immediately leave the country after overstaying amid stalled negotiations to end the war between both nations.[737]
September 29
The US sanctions ten people and entities in various jurisdictions that have acquired weapons and their parts for Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics.[738]
The X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain closes permanently following a series of lawsuits alleging brain injuries.[739]
September 30
The Trump administration concludes the withdrawal of US soldiers from their final bases in Iraq, marking the end of the US-led coalition's war against ISIL.[740]
A US defense contract for counter-drone systems is awarded to the Israeli company SMARTSHOOTER.[741]
Syria is removed from the US munitions export prohibition list.[742]
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirms that the American military will reduce 20% of its generals and admirals.[743]
The Office of Religious Affairs is established.[744]
The United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit temporarily halts the execution of Christa Gail Pike, but the U.S. Supreme Court later allows it to proceed. Pike survives two doses of pentobarbital and is hospitalized, prompting Tennessee governor Bill Lee to suspend the state's remaining 2026 execution and order an independent review.[745]
An immigration judge rules that Trump can deport the Palestinian-born leader of Wisconsin's largest mosque—an outspoken advocate of Palestinian rights—who does not have a criminal record in the US, where he has lived since 1993 on national security grounds, citing his imprisonment in Israel in 1988 after being convicted of throwing stones at Israeli military personnel in the West Bank.[746]
The United States Senate confirms Keith Sonderling as the 31st United States secretary of labor by a 47–41 vote.[747][748]
October[edit]
October 1
The US imposes new sanctions on Iran, targeting rail, automotive, manufacturing, and steel sectors, as well as overseas suppliers, saying that the goal is to economically isolate the Iranian government.[749]
The U.S. military starts sending about 9,000 soldiers to the Middle East on naval ships, such as the USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group and the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group.[750]
October 2: Alabama state representative Brett Easterbrook is arrested as a part of a sting.
October 2
The US imposes sanctions on Hamas' financing network, which includes two French-based funds.[751]
Alabama state representative Brett Easterbrook is arrested on charges of first-degree human trafficking and prostitution as part of a sting. At least a dozen other men are arrested.[752]
October 3 – Trump establishes a task force to examine the risks and opportunities of AI and recommend what role the federal government should play in overseeing the technology without compromising competitiveness with China.[753]
October 4
Two people are killed while 35 others are injured in a block party shooting in Vienna, Georgia.[754]
The State Department announces the expulsion of two members of the Iranian delegation who attended the recent United Nations General Assembly after they ignored an order to leave the country long after the General Assembly had ended.[755]
Trump withdraws all U.S. bombers from RAF Fairford, a British air base targeted by an attack that the UK linked to the Iranian government, due to urgent concerns about a potentially complex drone attack ordered by the IRGC as part of a plot to target the aircraft and kill American soldiers at RAF Fairford, which is loosely modeled after Ukraine's Operation Spiderweb.[756][757]
The FBI arrests Chinese American Wanying Zhang at Los Angeles International Airport for allegedly acting as an unregistered agent of China and surveilling the family of President of Taiwan Lai Ching-te in the United States.[758]
October 5
Responding to diesel price spikes tied to the conflict in Iran, Trump signs Executive Order 14435, permitting highway use of dyed diesel and deferring the 24.4-cent federal excise tax through 31 December.[759][760]
The Trump administration authorizes a $1 billion munitions sale to the UAE for up to 10,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon Systems, as well as a $400 million sale of "repair and return services" for Patriot missiles to Kuwait.[761]
Trump states that he remains "always open" to direct negotiations with Tehran.[762]
The US announces that foreign financial institutions doing business with Iran may be sanctioned without warning.[763]
October 6
Paramount Skydance completes its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, in one of the largest media mergers in history. The deal combines two of Hollywood's largest film studios with major television and streaming businesses including CBS, CNN, HBO and Paramount+, with the combined company renamed Skydance Corporation.[764]
Trump authorizes execution by firing squad for the Fort Hood attacker Nidal Hasan.[765]
The US destroys an Iranian-connected boat conducting surveillance after its crew was safely evacuated.[766]
October 7
The US and Greece agree on a coordinated security framework for counterterrorism information sharing among respective law enforcement agencies.[767]
The Wall Street Journal reports that U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle asked Republican donor Eric Deters to pay off $100,000 in credit card debt in exchange for access to the Trump administration, six days before her July 2025 Senate confirmation hearing. Guilfoyle's attorney said that any payments from Deters were for appearances.[768]
October 8
The US begins direct negotiations with the military junta of Myanmar while continuing sanctions against its leader, Min Aung Hlaing, for human rights violations, notably the Rohingya genocide.[769]
The US imposes additional sanctions on Iran's shadow fleet.[770]
Trump instructs the Pentagon to prepare military options in case active combat operations against Iran resume even as he said on that day that strikes would not renew prior to the midterm elections on November 3.[771][772]
October 9: 45-year-old Matthew Stone Sr. carries out a mass shooting which kills 9 people in Erie, Pennsylvania.
October 9
The US sanctions the International Criminal Court, stating that it will never allow the court to prosecute American soldiers.[773] The sanctions occurred after the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to former ICC judge Navi Pillay, and Trump criticized the decision on Truth Social.[774]
During a White House event, Trump declares that the war with Iran will "be over soon, one way or the other," suggesting that the almost eight-month-old conflict would either be resolved diplomatically or militarily.[775]
Trump announces that he secured Russian president Vladimir Putin's agreement to release diesel into U.S. and worldwide markets.[776]
Trump names Katie Zacharia as the new White House Press Secretary, succeeding Karoline Leavitt.[777]
Nine people are killed in a gun attack in Erie, Pennsylvania.[778]
October 10
Hundreds of thousands of Americans in Alabama and the Florida panhandle are without electricity after Hurricane Isaias hits the U.S. Gulf Coast. Trump cancels his intentions to attend a football match between the University of Georgia and the University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa, citing a desire not to impede emergency response operations, and declares a state of emergency in Alabama and Florida.[779][780]
The American military announces that it disabled a cargo ship attempting to violate its naval blockade of Iran.[781]
The Justice Department announces that it is probing whether major television networks breached federal antitrust laws by collectively refusing to cover the White House.[782]
October 12
Robert Hall and Michael Woodford are awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.[783]
Department of Homeland Security agents search the home of representative Ilhan Omar in Washington, D.C., as part of an "ongoing investigation".[784]
October 13
October 2026 white powder incident: An unmarked white powder is mailed, alongside threats, to dozens of state election officials and members of Congress, sparking fears of anthrax. The powders are later shown to be salt or yeast.
Following a request from Trump, Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns. Her resignation comes following multiple reports on her conduct, including one alleging that Guilfoyle asked a Republican donor to pay off her credit card.[785]
Former gang boss Duane "Keffe D" Davis is sentenced to 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur.[786]
Trump says the US will make a decision on Iran "very soon", describing it as a "failed country" and claiming its inflation has reached 300%.[787] His remarks coincide with reports that Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu urged renewed military action against Iran before the 27 October Israeli election, which Netanyahu's office denies.[788]
October 14 – Israel agrees to purchase 12 Boeing Apache helicopters.[789]
October 15
Authorities investigate letters containing "suspicious substances" mailed to congressional and election offices, suggestive of a similar threat in 2023.[790]
The US issues new sanctions against Iran, targeting 16 individuals and 10 entities.[791]
A mass shooting occurs outside an elementary school in Oregon killing four people, including three children.[792]
October 16 – Katie Zacharia is fired after just five days as White House Press Secretary.[793]
October 18 – Ukrainian president Zelenskyy says that the United States has started sharing intelligence again with Ukraine.[794]
October 19
Trump introduces the $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program, which will deliver one-time emergency financial aid to U.S. farmers struggling with record-high production expenses during the peak of the harvest season.[795]
The Supreme Court rejects a bid to restore a plea deal for Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the suspected 9/11 mastermind.[796]
Trump authorizes the creation of a National Institutes of Health division and a new White House task force to "advance the cause of women's health".[797]
October 20 – Trump signs an act into law designating the Chiricahua National Monument near Willcox, Arizona, as a national park, the first new national park in six years.[798]
October 21: pro-Israel lobbying group AIPAC announces that they will no longer be endorsing political candidates and making direct political action committee contributions.
October 21
Russian president Vladimir Putin announces the release of Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired American teacher who had been imprisoned by Moscow on charges of serving as a foreign combatant for Ukraine.[799]
The U.S. sanctions a Panama- and Greece-based law firm, stating that it facilitated Iran's shadow fleet for years and indirectly supported the Iranian government's capacity to produce income to fund its nuclear program.[800]
The Pentagon and Lockheed Martin reach a 10-year agreement to manufacture 850 F-35 Lightning II fighter jets.[801]
The pro-Israel lobby group AIPAC announces it will stop endorsing political candidates and making direct PAC contributions.[802]
October 22 – The Department of Justice accuses the Democrats of promoting a spoiler candidate with the same name as Republican incumbent candidate Dan Sullivan in the 2026 United States Senate election in Alaska to confuse voters.[803] The DOJ sues the state of Alaska to block the results if Senator Sullivan loses the election by a small margin.[804]
October 23
The White House announces that a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been agreed by President Putin and President Zelenskyy, mediated by First Lady Melania Trump.[805]
President Trump confirms that Starlink service has been restored for Ukraine.[806]
October 27 – A grand jury declines to indict Cassidy Hutchinson over her January 6 testimony.[807]
October 28: a parade on October 30 celebrating the Milwaukee Brewers winning the 2026 World Series.
October 28
In an attempt to resume peace talks, Vice President JD Vance sends a letter to Iranian National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei at Trump's directive.[808][809]
The District Court for the Eastern District of New York convicts a US woman of receiving Islamic State training after marrying an Islamic State militant at the age of 18.[810]
The Milwaukee Brewers defeat the Tampa Bay Rays to win the 2026 World Series, their first championship in franchise history.[811]
October 29
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fires Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the U.S. military's chief military planner.[812]
QatarEnergy announces a long-term liquefied natural gas procurement agreement with the United States until 2054.[813]
October 30
TRM Labs, an American blockchain analysis firm, reveals that North Korea's Bureau 121 was responsible for a $6.3 billion theft on cryptocurrency exchange Binance, the largest heist in history, prompting an investigation by the FBI and the US Secret Service.[814]
The Trump administration authorizes the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine.[815]
November[edit]
November 1: Democratic U.S. senator from Connecticut Chris Murphy is hospitalized after suffering a stroke whilst at his son's hockey game.
November 1: a Learjet 60 business jet crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida. All 9 people aboard the plane were killed in the crash.
November 1
Democratic senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut is hospitalized after suffering a stroke.[816]
A Learjet 60 crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board.[817]
Democratic representative Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic Abdul Al-Sayed in the Senate election in Michigan. Al-Sayed had previously defeated Stevens in the primaries. In response, Stevens's staff members resign and the Michigan Democratic Party revokes Stevens's party membership.[818]
November 2
Small-scale, "defensive" strikes are carried out by the US against Iranian positions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.[819]
A Washington state resident dies of bird flu.[820]
November 3: the 2026 United States midterm elections are held.
November 3
2026 United States midterm elections: in a blue wave, the Democratic Party wins majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.[821]
Trump announces that the US will terminate all military aid to Israel, totaling $4 billion per year, by the end of 2026, but will continue to sell military hardware.[822]
November 4
First Lady Melania Trump receives the Order of Princess Olga from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for her significant personal contribution to humanitarian relief efforts in Ukraine.[823]
The US imposes new sanctions on companies and individuals in India and Turkey with ties to the Iranian government.[824]
November 5
Harmeet Dhillon, the head of the Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division, resigns following the midterm elections.[825]
A Venezuelan man is detained near the White House on suspicion of plotting to assassinate Trump.[826]
Governor of California Gavin Newsom announces plans to commute the death sentences of all 548 prisoners on the state's death row to life imprisonment without parole, in what would be the largest mass commutation of death sentences in U.S. history. The move requires approval from the California Supreme Court for 382 of the prisoners.[827][828]
November 6
The number of measles cases in the United States exceeds 5,000 for the first time since 1991.[829][830]
Susie Wiles, Trump's White House Chief of Staff, is replaced by Stephen Miller, her deputy.[831]
Eight Canadian money services companies are sanctioned by the U.S. for dealing with the Iranian government.[832]
The US cuts off money exchanger MEXC due to transactions involving Iran, North Korea, and Russia.[833]
Thomas Markle, the father of Megan, Duchess of Sussex, is detained in Lakeland, Florida, for allegedly possessing sex abuse photographs of preadolescent girls, including images depicting himself with them.[834]
Trump declares that the US conducted "minor" strikes against Iran, targeting "a little bit of an anti-aircraft device."[835]
The Central Command (CENTCOM) announces a $20 million incentive "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear program.[836]
November 7 – CENTCOM expands its interdiction efforts against the Iranian government beyond its existing naval blockade by establishing Task Force Iron Gate to obstruct "illicit" shipments and weapons transit across land borders and the Caspian Sea.[837]
November 8 – Nvidia launches an investigation into allegations that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was targeted by Chinese intelligence, following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy.[838]
November 9 – The U.S. evacuates its military aircraft from RAF Mildenhall following a reported threat from Iran.[839]
November 10
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is relocated from his Washington, DC house to a military base due to threats against his life related to Operation Economic Outcast against the Iranian government.[840]
The House of Representatives blocks an impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth initiated by outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) by a vote of 211–204. The vote is along party lines with the exception of Massie, and eleven Democrats are no-shows for the vote.[841]
House Republicans elect Rep. Jim Jordan (R-OH) as their minority leader for the next Congress, succeeding outgoing Speaker of the House Mike Johnson. Jordan defeats Rep. Steve Scalise (R-LA) by 106–73 votes in a secret ballot.[842]
November 11: a building collapse in Brooklyn kills 8 and injures 18.
November 11: the SS United States is scuttled off the coast of Florida, becoming the largest artificial ocean reef in the world.
November 11
A three-story apartment building collapses in Brooklyn, New York City, killing eight people and injuring 17 others.[843]
A car crashes into a food stand near a bus stop in the North Hollywood section of Los Angeles, killing three people and seriously injuring three more.[844]
Democrat Scott Colom defeats incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi Senate election, becoming the state's first Black person elected to the United States Senate since 1874 and the first Democrat elected to the seat since 1982.[845]
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth awards a medal to a war memorial guard who reprimanded him.[846]
The SS United States, once the flagship ocean liner of United States Lines and holder of the Blue Riband, is sunk off the coast of Destin, Florida to become the world's largest artificial reef.[847]
November 12
Jensen Huang resigns as the CEO of Nvidia, following revelations of two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China.[848]
One person is killed and four are injured in a gun attack at and outside a fitness center in downtown Washington, D.C.[849]
Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) challenges Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY) for majority leader in the upcoming Congress. Van Hollen represents the progressive wing of the Democratic Party.[850]
2026 Microsoft outage: a global outage disrupts Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and Copilot, affecting businesses and government agencies worldwide for two days.[851]
November 13: John F. Kennedy International Airport during the nationwide grounding of all flights in the United States due to a communications outage. It is the largest nationwide grounding since 9/11.
November 13: the asphalt and bitumen tanker Atlantic Asphalt collides with the river cruise ship American Heritage in New Orleans, Louisiana.
November 13
The FBI announces that North Korea used fake video calls to steal $400 million in cryptocurrency.[852]
The International Criminal Court closes its investigations into suspected war crimes committed by US troops in Afghanistan, following institutional sanctions imposed by the US on the court.[853]
The FAA issues a nationwide ground stop for the first time since 9/11, due to a "telecommunications outage".[854]
2026 New Orleans ship collision: an oil tanker collides with the docked river boat American Heritage in New Orleans, Louisiana, injuring 32 people.[855]
A bomb is found at an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, after a "credible bomb threat" was called in. An evacuation is ordered for residents within a one-mile radius of the site, and some local events are cancelled.[856][857]
The United States officially loses its measles elimination status.[858]
November 14 – After a 22-hour orbital test flight, SpaceX successfully recovers its Starship vehicle with mechanical launch-tower arms at Starbase in Texas, marking the first-ever recovery of an orbital upper-stage spacecraft.[859][860]
November 16 – US intelligence detects potential Iranian plans for dirty bomb or chemical attacks against senior Trump administration officials in Washington, D.C, an allegation dismissed by Iran.[861][862][863]
November 16–17:
November 2026 technology outages: after the global Microsoft outage and the nationwide FAA ground stop, more technology outages occur in the United States. Several major U.S. national banks and financial services companies (including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and U.S. Bank) also experience service disruptions and outages beginning on November 16. Most of the banks' issues stem from disruptions to JPMorgan Chase systems.[864] The National Security Agency's internal communications network experiences an outage on November 17.[865][866] Apple also experiences an outage with several of its products and services on November 17.[867]
November 17
The U.S. military states that in response to an earlier Iranian drone attack that targeted a US radar installation at Isa Air Base in Bahrain, US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.[868][869]
A federal judge in Brooklyn sentences Pakistani national Asif Merchant to 27½ years imprisonment for plotting with the Iranian government to assassinate U.S. officials, including Trump, Biden, and Nikki Haley.[870][871]
Trump meets with the leaders of Australia, India, and Japan in Manila, Philippines, for the first Quadrilateral Security Dialogue summit of his second term, announcing multilateral agreements to secure critical mineral supply chains.[872][873]
Democrat Mary Peltola defeats incumbent Republican senator Dan Sullivan in the 2026 United States Senate election in Alaska, becoming the first Alaska Native elected to the United States Senate and the first Democrat to win a Senate election in the state since 2008.[874]
November 18 – NASA's Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object to reach a distance of one light-day (25.9 billion kilometres) from Earth, nearly 50 years after its launch in 1977. At this distance, radio signals take 24 hours to travel between Earth and the spacecraft.[875][876]
November 19: the APEC summit takes place in Shenzhen, China.
November 19
During the 2026 APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, Trump, CCP general secretary Xi Jinping, and Russian president Vladimir Putin hold their first-ever trilateral meeting and release a joint statement on energy supplies, nuclear non-proliferation, and UN reform.[877]
San Francisco-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic, developer of the Claude chatbot, makes its debut on the Nasdaq following an $81.3 billion initial public offering, the largest in history. The offering values the company at approximately $1.5 trillion, surpassing the previous IPO fundraising record set by SpaceX earlier in the year.[878][879]
Following widespread technological outages across the country, Trump removes National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross and appoints the Defense Department’s Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies as acting director.[880][881]
The FCC bans Chinese firms from direct access to United States phone numbers in a bid to curb robocalls.[882]
November 20
The US Treasury sanctions "trustees" who receive oil revenues for the Iranian government, adding that in many cases they have kept the funds for personal gain.[883]
The Nasdaq Composite falls 5.28% amid a widespread sell-off in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks, ending the week down 10% in one of its steepest weekly declines since March 2020. The S&P 500 also falls 3.7%, entering correction territory.[884]
A federal jury in Los Angeles convicts Jonathan Rinderknecht on two charges relating to the Palisades Fire of January 2025, which killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 structures. The fire was one of the most destructive in California's history.[885][886]
November 22 – The Democratic Party secures its largest House majority since 1992, after the race is called for Democrat Chuck Hubbard in North Carolina's 5th congressional district. His win, against Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx, takes the party's total number of seats to 258, with four midterm races yet to be called.[887]
November 23: Representative Jimmy Gomez resigns from Congress after it had been discovered that he had an extramarital affair with an aide and that he had also sexually assaulted another one.
November 23: a head-on bus collision in Columbus, Ohio injures 9 and kills both bus drivers.
November 23
Following his resignation on November 12, Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as its chief executive officer amid pressure from investors and Trump.[888] Trump states that the federal government saw no national security risk in Huang's return as Nvidia's CEO or evidence of unlawful conduct, while urging the company to continue its internal export-control compliance review.[889]
The US imposes sanctions on dozens of individuals related to the Iranian government's shadow banking networks.[890]
California representative Jimmy Gomez resigns from Congress after a House Ethics Committee report found that he had an extramarital affair with an aide and had sexually assaulted another one.[891]
The New York Court of Appeals rules 4–3 that major technology companies, including Meta and Google, are not civilly liable for the 2022 Buffalo shooting.[892]
A head-on bus collision in Columbus, Ohio kills two bus drivers and injures nine other people.[893]
November 24 – A federal jury in Brooklyn convicts Chinese telecommunications company Huawei on 10 of 12 criminal counts, including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and Iran sanctions violations, while acquitting it of racketeering and obstruction of justice.[894]
November 25: around 10,000 pounds of lead azide is detonated at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant.
November 25 – The U. S. Army detonates a 10,000 pound pile of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown (near Burlington). The detonation produces a major plume of lead-contaminated smoke, which will potentially affect eastern parts of Iowa, western portions of Illinois, as well as the entire Mississippi River going southward.[895]
November 25 – Organizers postpone the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City to November 28 due to a major nor'easter. This marks the first weather-related postponement in the event's history.[896]
Predicted and scheduled events[edit]
December[edit]
December 3 – Nidal Hasan is scheduled to be executed. If carried out, he would be the first sitting member of the United States Armed Forces to be executed since John A. Bennett was executed in 1961 for rape and attempted murder.[897]
